body:
## Confirmed player-visible defect
At FullHD 1920?1080, UI 100%, an angled camera drag started on the map resumes when the held middle/right button returns from a native HUD control to the canvas. Moving through the HUD should end that camera drag, consistent with the scene's existing cancellation handler.

### Actual native reproduction
1. Create a prison using the actual production client and pause it.
2. Open Build, with no placement tool armed.
3. Hold middle button and drag on uncovered map; the map pans normally.
4. Continue the same held gesture into the native Category selector.
5. Return to uncovered map while holding the button: the camera jumps/pans again.
6. Repeat with right button: the camera resumes turning on reentry.

Real DOM traces retain canvas mouseout, native SELECT ownership, and buttons 4/2 on return. Original production callbacks fail both native cases. The revised strict map-pixel comparison also fails both cases when only the corrected producer callback is removed; independent minimap viewport changes agree. Both negatives issue zero worker commands.

### Cause and scoped correction
The existing Phaser `pointerout` listener is GameObject-specific and is not emitted for canvas exit. Shipped MouseManager/InputPlugin emit `gameout(timeStamp, nativeMouseEvent)`. Stored middle-pan and right-turn IDs/anchors survive that event. The minimal correction clears only those four camera fields on `gameout`, preserving construction capture, retained hover and touch tracking.

Production source checkpoint: e3bd575b13 on codex/hud-camera-gameout-audit-20261002. Registered real-scene callback diagnostic: 5f234f1feb; native instrument/preservation checkpoint: 95f3570bdd.

### Evidence and restoration
- Original callback unit diagnostic: 2 RED / 4 valid controls GREEN.
- Final seven-case producer omission: 2 RED / 5 controls GREEN; byte-exact restoration 7 GREEN.
- Broad-cancel negative deliberately clears protected construction/touch state: 1 RED / 6 GREEN; exact restoration 7 GREEN.
- Revised native fixed cases: 2 GREEN (9.0s each).
- Actual producer omission: 2 RED (8.4s / 7.8s), at exact uncovered-map pixels; viewport changes independently.
- Exact source restoration and rebuild: 8 GREEN, including camera middle/right (8.9s / 9.1s), existing wall capture at FullHD 100%/200% and retained mirrored q0/q1 room preview at FullHD 100%/200%.
- Original 60/10-second case/expectation limits, one worker, zero Playwright retries; no new tracked config. All browser processes terminal, port5404 zero listeners.

### Honest instrument boundary
The first native attempt failed at an ambiguous Category selector and was not product evidence. An initial corrected-source full-canvas comparison also differed because the canvas bounding rectangle includes composited hovered HUD controls: every fixed-image difference was inside x1569..1909, while uncovered-map pixels were identical. Both raw attempts are retained. The revised test compares exact pixels in an independently hit-tested uncovered map region, with independent minimap styles; no tolerance was introduced. The original producer fails that same assertion.

### Nonduplicate check and limits
Fresh REST all-state searches for gameout (0), camera reentry (0), and camera drag HUD (19); read #878, #1971 and #1935. #1935 covers blur/pointercancel; #1971/#878 cover left-button construction capture, which stays green. This report concerns the distinct actual canvas-exit camera event.

Acceptance covers mouse middle/right angled-camera exit/reentry at UI100%, ordinary/fresh camera drag, and the named protected construction fixtures at UI100%/200%. Touch hardware, browser-window exit, Save/Load, fixed-renderer turn/pan, main CI and deployment are not claimed. Published detailed logs, raw traces and images follow in the scoped research receipt.

title: Angled camera middle/right drag resumes after leaving canvas through native HUD controls
